Privacy Policy

Effective November 27, 2026 · Android version

Boreum (“the app”) is a Korean lunar calendar you can use without signing up. This policy explains what information the app handles, where it is kept, and what information goes to Google for ads.

This policy applies to the Android app from Google Play. For the iPhone and iPad app, see the iOS Privacy Policy.

  • No sign-up, no loginThe app never asks for your name, email or phone number.
  • Your dates stay on your deviceAnniversaries, saved days and settings are stored on the device and never uploaded.
  • No server of oursThe developer does not receive or keep any of your information. There are no analytics tools in the app.
  • Ads by Google AdMobWhile you use the free plan, Google processes the information needed for ads. With Pro, the app stops requesting ads.

1. Information the developer collects

None. The developer does not collect any personal information, such as your name, contact details, date of birth, location or device identifiers, and the app sends nothing to the developer's own servers. The app contains no usage statistics or analytics tools.

The app never asks for a birth date, birth time or gender, and makes no readings about individuals. Calendar and almanac information is calculated from the date alone.

2. Information stored only on your device

The app keeps the following on your device only (in the app's private storage), so that its features work. None of it is sent to the developer.

Saved daysDate, title, note
AnniversariesTitle, type (birthday, memorial rite, anniversary, other), lunar or solar date and leap-month flag, year of birth, year of passing or first year (if you enter it), reminder timing, note
SettingsLanguage, text size, theme and appearance, calendar display options, reminder time, sound and haptics, and so on
App recordsWhether Pro is unlocked (a cached value for display), when and how often ads were shown (used only to keep ads infrequent), when a temporary pass from a rewarded ad expires, and a list of events handed to your Calendar app (to avoid duplicates)

Deleting the app deletes this information. If Android backup (backup to your Google Account) is turned on, it may be included in your device backup in your Google Account, which Google manages, and restored when you reinstall the app or set up a new device with the same Google Account. That backup is stored in your Google Account, and the developer cannot see it. You can turn backup on or off in the backup menu of your device settings.

Anniversary reminders include the anniversary's title, so depending on your device settings it may appear on the lock screen. To hide it, change how notifications appear on the lock screen in Settings › Notifications (menu names vary slightly by device).

3. Device features

Calendar (no permission)

When you tap “Add to Calendar”, the app hands the events you choose (title, date, note, alert) to the Calendar app on your device. For a single event, your Calendar app opens its new-event screen; for several events, or events with alerts, the app creates a calendar file (.ics) and hands it to your Calendar app or to an app you choose. You save the events in that app. The app does not ask for calendar permission, and it cannot read your existing events or write to your calendar directly. Added events become part of that Calendar app, and whether they sync depends on your calendar settings.

Notifications (local)

Anniversary and solar-term reminders are local notifications scheduled on the device; no push server is used. On Android 13 and later, the app asks for notification permission once, when you first turn on a reminder. You can turn notifications off anytime in the app's notification settings on your device. So that reminders still arrive after you restart the device, the app reschedules them once the device has finished starting up.

Sharing

The Share button opens the Android share sheet. The information goes only to the app you choose; Boreum does not keep or send it anywhere else.

Saving images

When you save the Son-free year view image with “Save Image”, the app adds the image to your device's gallery. It can only add images; it does not use any permission to read your photos. On Android 10 and later no permission is requested; on Android 8 and 9, the system may ask for storage permission when you save.

Android permissions the app uses

NotificationsPOST_NOTIFICATIONS — shows anniversary and solar-term reminders. Asked once on Android 13 and later.
Run at startupRECEIVE_BOOT_COMPLETED — reschedules reminders after the device restarts.
VibrationVIBRATE — used for haptics you turn on in Settings.
Internet and network stateINTERNET, ACCESS_NETWORK_STATE — used only for ads and the ad consent check.
Advertising IDAD_ID — lets the Google ads SDK read the advertising ID (section 4).
BillingBILLING — buys and restores Pro through Google Play billing (section 6).
OthersPermissions declared by the Google ads SDK and the reminder scheduling library (such as Android ad services permissions and permissions needed to schedule work). You are not asked for these.

The app does not use location, contacts, camera, microphone or calendar permissions, or any permission to read photos and videos.

4. Ads (Google AdMob)

While you use the free (Basic) plan, the Google Mobile Ads SDK from Google LLC shows ads. To select, show and measure ads, Google may collect and process the following through the app:

  • Device identifiers: the Android advertising ID (unless you have deleted it in your device settings) and the app set ID (a device identifier scoped to one developer's apps)
  • Coarse location: an approximate area estimated from your IP address (no precise location)
  • Advertising data: such as the ads you saw and tapped
  • Product interaction: such as app launches and ad-related taps
  • Diagnostics: performance data and crash logs from the ads SDK

Google handles this information under How Google uses information from sites or apps that use its services and the Google Privacy Policy.

Advertising ID (Android)

Android has no tracking permission prompt like the one on iPhone, so the app does not ask whether to allow tracking. Instead, Google may use your device's advertising ID for ads. You can reset or delete the advertising ID anytime in Settings › Privacy › Ads (on some devices, Settings › Google › Ads). If you delete it, a string of zeros is passed instead and the advertising ID is not used, and every feature of the app keeps working. On some devices, the same menu also lets you change ad privacy settings (such as ad topics and ad measurement).

Ad consent (EEA, UK, Switzerland and similar regions)

Where the law requires consent, Google's consent form (User Messaging Platform) appears before any ad is requested. To check this, the app contacts Google's servers at launch, and Google determines your region from your IP address. Users in those regions can change or withdraw their choice anytime from the ad privacy option that appears in the app's Settings.

Ad rating and Pro

  • Ads are limited to content suitable for all ages (rating G).
  • After you buy Pro, the app stops requesting ads, and from the next launch it does not start the ads SDK at all. A temporary pass earned from a rewarded ad does not remove ads.

5. International transfer of ad-related information

The ad-related information in section 4 is collected directly by Google and processed outside Korea. As required by Korea's Personal Information Protection Act, here are the details.

RecipientGoogle LLC (contact: Google privacy help)
CountriesThe United States and other countries where Google processes data
ItemsDevice identifiers (the Android advertising ID unless deleted, and the app set ID), coarse location estimated from IP address, advertising data, product interaction, diagnostics
When and howSent over the network when the free app checks ad consent or requests and shows ads
PurposeServing and measuring ads, preventing fraud, improving the ad service
RetentionUnder Google's Privacy Policy
How to refuseDelete the advertising ID in your device settings (stops its use); in consent regions, withdraw consent from the ad privacy option; or buy Pro (stops ad requests). The app's core features keep working either way.

6. In-app purchase

Pro is sold through Google Play's billing system, which processes the payment with your Google Account. The developer never receives payment details such as card numbers; the app only checks whether Pro was purchased, using the Google Play Billing Library. Restoring a purchase also goes through the same Google Account.

7. Children

The app is for a general audience and is not directed at children. The developer does not collect personal information from anyone, including children, and ads are limited to content suitable for all ages (G). Parents can use Google Play's purchase authentication settings or Google Family Link to restrict in-app purchases.

8. Retention and deletion

The developer keeps no user information. You can delete anniversaries and saved days in the app, and deleting the app removes everything stored on the device. A copy included in your device backup can be managed in your Google Account's backup settings. Ad-related information processed by Google is kept and deleted under Google's policies.

9. Your rights

Because the developer holds no information about you, there is nothing on our side to access, correct or delete. You can view, edit and delete the information on your device within the app. You can change your ad choices as described in section 4, and exercise rights over information held by Google under Google's policies. If you have questions, contact us below.

10. Security

The app does not send your records off the device, and information stored on the device is protected by Android's per-app storage isolation and device encryption. Since the developer receives no user information, there is no separate system that stores it.

11. Changes to this policy

If this policy changes, we will post the new version and its effective date on this page, and mention significant changes in the app's update notes.
